preconditions.description: Number of test cases is between 1 and 5.
Number of cities is between 2 and 5000.
Number of roads proposed by other companies is between 1 and 20000.
Number of roads proposed by Chef's company is between 1 and 20000.
Cost of each road is between 0 and 1000000000.

postconditions.expression: return_value == 'Impossible' or isinstance(return_value, tuple) and len(return_value) == 2 and isinstance(return_value[0], int) and isinstance(return_value[1], int)
postconditions.description: Output is either 'Impossible' or a tuple of two integers.

postconditions.expression: return_value != 'Impossible' implies all(cities are connected by exactly one path of roads)
postconditions.description: If not 'Impossible', the chosen roads form a spanning tree connecting all cities.

postconditions.expression: return_value != 'Impossible' implies return_value[0] == sum(costs of Chef's roads in the chosen subset)
postconditions.description: The first integer in the output is the total cost of Chef's roads in the chosen subset.

postconditions.expression: return_value != 'Impossible' implies return_value[1] == sum(costs of all roads in the chosen subset)
postconditions.description: The second integer in the output is the total cost of all roads in the chosen subset.

postconditions.expression: return_value != 'Impossible' implies for any other valid subset of roads, return_value[0] >= sum(costs of Chef's roads in that subset)
postconditions.description: The chosen subset yields the maximum profit among all valid subsets.

postconditions.expression: return_value != 'Impossible' implies for any other valid subset of roads yielding the same maximum profit, return_value[1] <= sum(costs of all roads in that subset)
postconditions.description: Among subsets yielding the same maximum profit, the chosen subset has the minimum total cost.
